subject: Temporary residency handoff & KMS escrow — timeline and asks
body:
From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.com>
To: Sara Patel <sara.patel@acmehealth.com>
Cc: karthik.iyer@redwood.com, marcus.lin@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 12 Mar 2026 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Temporary residency handoff & KMS escrow — timeline and asks

Hi Sara,

Thanks again for the conversation earlier today. To keep momentum on the residency commitment and the limited temporary cross-region processing window we discussed, can you confirm the minimal timeline you need from contract signature to certificate-of-acceptance for your DPO? Specifically: 

- Do you require a separate DPA Annex for the 72-hour transient-hop exception, or will a clause in the main DPA suffice?
- Is Acme comfortable with a KMS-escrow workflow (customer-held wrap key, Redwood rotates ephemeral data keys, Redwood stores wrapped key in an escrow vault only accessible under failover conditions)?
- Any SLAs for notification/time-to-return if a transient hop is triggered (we suggested 4 hours notification + 72h max processing window)?

Attached: short playbook describing our temporary-handoff pattern + a CSV of current subprocessors we anticipate touching logs/telemetry during the window. I want to share a proposed internal timeline then tag Marcus and Karthik for technical confirmation.

Next steps I'd like to propose:
1) You confirm whether Annex or inline clause is preferred by Monique (DPO).
2) We provide a redlined DPA clause and example escrow flow (by EOD Friday).
3) Agree on ops checklist — test vector and telemetry sampling for the first production cutover.

If you prefer a quick call tomorrow morning (30 min), we can run through the playbook and the escrow steps.

Best,
Jasmine Liu
Senior Security & Solutions
Redwood Inference

--- Attachment stubs attached: residency_playbook_short.pdf (6 pages), subprocessor_roster_20260312.csv (roster), DPA_draft_v1.1.pdf (skeleton) ---


From: Sara Patel <sara.patel@acmehealth.com>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.com>
Cc: security@acmehealth.com
Date: Fri, 13 Mar 2026 08:42:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Temporary residency handoff & KMS escrow — timeline and asks

Hi Jasmine —

Thanks for the summary. A few quick clarifications from our side: 

1) Our DPO prefers a short Annex that can be attached to the standard DPA so internal stakeholders see the temporary-hop conditions explicitly.
2) KMS escrow conceptually works, but we need to understand exactly who controls the unwrap operation and under which conditions Redwood would request a customer key unwrap (e.g., operational failover vs. incident response).
3) The 4h notification + 72h window seems reasonable as a maximum; however, Monique has asked for a more granular breakdown (notice, approval, and auditability).

Can you share what telemetry we would see during a transient hop (types of logs, retention, and redaction of PHI)? Also please add the contact for the escrow vault operations so our security team can do an intake.

Sara
Sara Patel
Head of Security, Acme Health
security@acmehealth.com


From: karthik.iyer@redwood.com <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.com>, Sara Patel <sara.patel@acmehealth.com>
Cc: marcus.lin@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 13 Mar 2026 11:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Temporary residency handoff & KMS escrow — timeline and asks

Sara / Jasmine —

Looping in a few technical specifics to answer the unwrap/escrow questions and to propose language for the Annex: 

- Escrow design: customer provides a wrap key held in their KMS (we store the wrapped data-encryption-key; unwrap requires a two-party operation: Redwood ops + customer vault approval via a signed API call). We can add an audit-only path so unwrap requests are rejected unless explicit customer approval is present (recommended for regulated health customers).
- Failure modes: for short failover (e.g., regional outage), Redwood can run in a pre-authorized limited-read mode for 72h where only tokenized/obfuscated telemetry is allowed to leave the region. Full unwrap and access to plaintext requires the customer approval flow. 
- Telemetry: we surface request-level traces (request_id, model_id, timestamp, region_source, region_destination), sampling of input hashes (not full text), and system logs (pod/node ids). PHI is never shipped in plaintext in telemetry; we can include a finer redaction policy in the Annex. Retention default is 30 days for transient hop logs, configurable to 7/14/30.

Suggested Annex clause language (short excerpt) — feel free to copy into your legal channel: 
"Temporary Cross-Region Processing Annex: Redwood will not transfer customer content outside the designated region except under the conditions described. For transient hops (operational failover or capacity reroute), Redwood may perform limited processing in a second region for a maximum of 72 hours. Such processing will be restricted to tokenized request traces and encrypted processing buffers. Any decryption of customer content from escrowed keys requires a documented customer approval event and will be logged and auditable via the escrow vault audit trail."

I also attach a one-page ops checklist that Marcus helped draft (see residency_playbook_short.pdf). Marcus: can you confirm the proposed notification flow (we suggest automated alert -> 1hr ops callback -> 4hr formal notice + 72h processing) and whether we can commit to the 4h notice SLA?

—Karthik


From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.com>, karthik.iyer@redwood.com, Sara Patel <sara.patel@acmehealth.com>
Date: Sun, 15 Mar 2026 17:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Temporary residency handoff & KMS escrow — timeline and asks

Jasmine / Karthik / Sara —

Confirming the ops timeline and a couple of practical constraints: 

- Automated alert -> 1hr ops callback -> 4hr formal notice is achievable for targeted accounts (we'd need the account to be on a pinned incident routing list). For general-hosted customers the 4h window is aspirational but not guaranteed. Given Acme's expected commit level (Dedicated/DPA annex), we can add you to the prioritized routing list.
- Escrow unwrap events: engineering can instrument an escrow approval API that requires a signed customer token. Unwraps will be gated behind the approval flow and logged into our escrow audit (immutable). We can provide the audit stream to Acme for a rolling 90-day retention export if required.
- Subprocessor notes: during a transient hop, only a minimal set of infra subprocessors (cloud infra + edge-cdn) will be invoked; third-party model-hosting subprocessors are not. That's reflected in subprocessor_roster_20260312.csv.

Action items:
1) Jasmine -> send a redlined Annex and DPA draft to Monique (Acme DPO) by EOD Monday (we aim to send DPA_draft_v1.1.pdf attached).
2) Sara -> confirm Annex acceptance or list required edits; provide approval contact for your escrow vault ops.
3) Marcus/Karthik -> prepare a short ops runbook and an audit export sample to attach to the Annex.

I'll follow up with the runbook and example audit export next week.

Thanks,
Marcus Lin
Principal Product Ops, Redwood Inference
